input: …it should be noted that the overrun currently stands at 3 weeks, and the principal cause of this position can be traced to the EPC re-forecast, under which the remaining work was repriced following a remeasurement of the quantities associated with the packages that have already been installed on site. The rates that were carried in the earlier forecast were not, in the event, supported by the remeasured quantities, and the resulting difference has manifested itself in relation to packages that had previously been reported as settled. In order to address this situation, the mitigation that is proposed consists of a single, comprehensive re-planning of the remaining packages against the repriced forecast, which will be owned by the project board. Under this approach, the remaining work will be re-baselined in a single exercise, as a complete set, rather than being corrected on a piecemeal, package-by-package basis as each individual account is closed. Until such time as the project board has received the re-plan, the position that is reported here will remain as stated, and those packages that are still to run will continue to be managed against a baseline that has, in effect, already been superseded by the re-forecast. It is also important to recognise that the exposure lies not in the packages that have already been closed, but rather in those that remain open, which continue to carry the earlier rates as the basis of their reported position…
target: …the overrun now stands at 3 weeks, and the cause sits with the EPC re-forecast, which repriced the remaining work after the quantities on the installed packages were remeasured on site. The earlier forecast carried rates that the remeasurement did not support, and the difference has come through against packages that had been reported as settled. The mitigation proposed is a single re-plan of the remaining packages against the repriced forecast, owned by the project board: the remaining work is re-baselined once, as a set, rather than corrected package by package as each account closes. The re-plan also settles the order in which the open packages are remeasured where site records are incomplete, so that no package is left carrying rates from the earlier forecast by default. Until the project board has the re-plan, the position reported here stays as stated, and packages still to run continue against a baseline the re-forecast has already moved. The exposure sits in the packages still open, not in the ones already closed: those still open carry the old rates as the basis of their reported position, and further commitments against them would extend the overrun before it is visible in any report. The re-plan has to reach the open packages before their remaining costs are committed, and it has to carry the repriced rates into the forecast for the work that follows them, so that the position reported for the next period rests on rates the remeasurement supports…
